tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read file contents. Supports text, images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP), PDFs, and Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb).

Parameters:
- path: File path (relative/absolute, supports ~/)
- offset: Start line (1-indexed)
- limit: Max lines
- mode: "normal", "head", "tail"
- encoding: utf-8 (default), utf-16le, latin1, ascii

Auto-detects images, PDFs, and notebooks. Provides syntax highlighting and handles large files.
Emit multiple read tool calls in one turn when you need parallel reads; the runtime will execute them concurrently—no batch wrapper required.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

mode.description: Reading mode: normal offset/limit, head, or tail

lineNumbers.description: Prefix output lines with line numbers

wrapInCodeFence.description: Wrap text output in a Markdown code fence

asBase64.description: Return binary files as base64 instead of text

language.description: Language identifier for the code fence (overrides auto-detection)

encoding.description: Text encoding for the file (default: utf-8). Use latin1 for legacy files.

tools.name: list
tools.description:
List files and directories using glob patterns with filtering and sorting.

Parameters:
- path: Directory to list (default: current directory)
- pattern: Glob pattern (default: *)
- excludePatterns: Array of patterns to exclude (e.g., ['node_modules/**', 'dist/**'])
- limit: Max entries (1-500, default: 200)
- maxDepth: Directory depth limit (0 = unlimited)
- includeHidden: Include dotfiles
- includeMetadata: Include size and timestamps
- sortBy: name, type, size, mtime
- format: text or json

Examples:
  {path: "src", pattern: "**/*.ts"}
  {excludePatterns: ["node_modules/**", "*.log"]}

path.description: Directory to list (relative or absolute). Defaults to current directory.

pattern.description: Glob pattern relative to the directory. Defaults to *

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (1-500). Defaults to 200.

maxDepth.description: Maximum directory depth to traverse (0 = unlimited)

includeMetadata.description: Include file size and modified timestamps

excludePatterns.description: Array of glob patterns to exclude (e.g., ['node_modules/**', '*.log', 'dist/**'])

tools.name: oracle
tools.description: Summon the Seer - a mystical systems advisor that foresees consequences of complex engineering decisions. Ideal for architecture reviews, deep debugging, and strategic guidance.

task.description: The task or question you want the Oracle to help with. Be specific about what kind of guidance, review, or planning you need.

model.description: Optional model id to use for the Oracle (must be available in your configured models). Defaults to a reasoning-capable model such as o3-mini.

context.description: Optional context about the current situation, what you've tried, or background information that would help the Oracle provide better guidance.

files.description: Optional list of specific file paths that the Oracle should examine as part of its analysis.

tools.name: painter
tools.description: Generate or edit images via an image model (default gpt-image-2). Use for UI mockups, app icons, illustrations, and editing existing images (e.g. redacting a screenshot). Outputs are persisted to disk and returned as absolute paths; reference them by path in later turns. Requires OPENAI_API_KEY.

mode.description: generate = create a new image from a text prompt. edit = modify one or more existing images using a prompt (and optional mask).

prompt.description: The image prompt. For edit mode, describe the desired change. Be concrete about subject, style, composition, and any text to render.

images.description: Edit mode only. 1-3 absolute or workspace-relative paths to input images to edit.

mask.description: Edit mode only. Path to a mask image; transparent regions mark areas the model may change. Omit to edit the whole image. Mutually exclusive with maskRegion (which synthesizes the mask for you).

maskRegion.description: Edit mode only. A pixel bounding box; the mask is synthesized automatically (transparent = editable). Coordinates outside the image are clipped.

maskSize.description: Explicit input image dimensions, used only for mask synthesis when the input is not a PNG and Sharp is unavailable. Optional.

size.description: Output size. Standard: 1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, 1792x1024, 1024x1792, or auto. gpt-image-2 also accepts arbitrary WxH divisible by 16 with aspect ratio 1:3 to 3:1.

quality.description: Output quality. Higher quality is slower and more expensive. Defaults to auto.

n.description: Number of images to produce (1-4). Defaults to 1.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search for files by glob pattern using fd. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Use this for fast file discovery across large codebases.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

tools.name: extract_document
tools.description: Download a document from a URL and extract its text. Supports PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, common text formats, and optional MarkItDown-backed Markdown conversion when available. Use this when you need text from a linked document.

url.description: HTTP(S) URL of a document (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, or text file)

maxChars.description: Maximum characters of extracted text to return

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Find text across files using ripgrep with optional globbing and context controls.

Output modes (outputMode parameter):
- "content": Show matching lines with file:line:content format (default)
- "files": List only file paths containing matches (fast for finding files)
- "count": Show match counts per file (useful for gauging scope)

Modifiers:
- invertMatch: Show lines that do NOT match
- onlyMatching: Show only the matched text (content mode only)
- headLimit: Limit output to first N entries (useful for sampling)

Examples:
  {pattern: "TODO", outputMode: "files"}  → list files containing TODO
  {pattern: "function", outputMode: "count"}  → count functions per file
  {pattern: "^#", invertMatch: true}  → lines not starting with #

parameters.description: Use either context or before/after context options, not both.

items.description: Multiple directories or files to search

literal.description: Treat the pattern as a literal string (--fixed-strings).

context.description: Show this many lines of context before and after (-C).

beforeContext.description: Show this many lines of context before each match (-B).

afterContext.description: Show this many lines of context after each match (-A).

cwd.description: Working directory to run ripgrep from

outputMode.description: Output mode: 'content' shows matching lines (default), 'files' lists only file paths, 'count' shows match counts per file.

format.description: Output format for content mode. JSON not supported with files/count modes.

invertMatch.description: Show lines that do NOT match the pattern (--invert-match).

onlyMatching.description: Only show the matched text, not the entire line (--only-matching). Only works with content mode.

headLimit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries. Useful for sampling large result sets.

tools.name: parallel_ripgrep
tools.description: Search for multiple patterns simultaneously. Runs ripgrep queries in parallel, automatically merges overlapping line ranges, and returns consolidated content. Ideal for finding related code (e.g., function definitions AND usages) or multiple related patterns without duplicate context.

patterns.description: Regex patterns to search for in parallel (1-10). Results are merged when matches overlap.

items.description: Multiple directories or files to search

literal.description: Treat patterns as literal strings, not regex (--fixed-strings)

context.description: Lines of context before and after each match (-C)

beforeContext.description: Lines of context before each match (-B)

afterContext.description: Lines of context after each match (-A)

headLimit.description: Max number of merged line ranges to return

tools.name: diff
tools.description: Inspect git diffs with optional staging, revision, and path filters.

parameters.description: Cannot request both name-only and word-diff output (diff mode only).

staged.description: Show staged (index) changes instead of working tree modifications.

range.description: Git revision or range (for example HEAD~1..HEAD). Overrides staged/worktree scope.

context.description: Number of context lines to include (git -U).

stat.description: Include a summary (--stat) alongside the patch.

wordDiff.description: Highlight changes at the word level (--word-diff=color).

ignoreWhitespace.description: Ignore whitespace changes (--ignore-space-change). Useful for comparing reformatted code.

ignoreBlankLines.description: Ignore changes that only add or remove blank lines (--ignore-blank-lines).

anyOf.description: Limit diff to a specific path

items.description: Multiple paths to include in the diff

tools.name: bash
tools.description:
Execute bash commands.

Usage guidelines:
- ALWAYS quote paths with spaces: cd "/path with spaces"
- DO NOT use: find, grep, cat, head, tail, ls (use search, read, list tools instead)
- Prefer rg over grep if you must search
- Chain commands with ';' or '&&', avoid cd
- Use 'gh' CLI for GitHub operations (gh pr create, gh issue list, gh repo view)

Supports interpolation in command:
- ${cwd} - current working directory
- ${home} - user home directory
- ${env.VAR} - environment variable

Timeout: 90s default, 600s max. Output truncates at 40KB.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

cwd.description: Working directory for the command (relative or absolute)

env.description: Additional environment variables for the command

runInBackground.description: Run command as a managed background task (use background_tasks tool to inspect/stop)

tools.name: background_tasks
tools.description: Run commands in the background and manage their lifecycle.

command.description: Command to run in the background

shell.description: Run the command through the system shell (allows pipes/redirection). Defaults to false for direct execution.

env.description: Additional environment variables for the command

maxAttempts.description: Maximum number of restart attempts when the task exits with a non-zero status

delayMs.description: Delay in milliseconds between restart attempts

maxDelayMs.description: Upper bound for exponential backoff delays

jitterRatio.description: Random jitter ratio applied to restart delays (0-1)

logSizeLimit.description: Per-task log size limit in bytes (overrides default). Minimum 0, maximum 50MB.

logSegments.description: Number of gzip-compressed log segments to retain when rotating.

retentionMs.description: Milliseconds to retain finished task metadata and logs before cleanup.

maxRssKb.description: Maximum resident set size in kilobytes before the task is terminated (0 disables).

maxCpuMs.description: Maximum combined user+system CPU time in milliseconds before termination (0 disables).

taskId.description: Identifier of the background task to stop

lines.description: Number of log lines to show

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description:
Apply an OpenAI/Codex apply_patch block directly.

Parameters:
- patch: Patch text using *** Begin Patch / *** End Patch with Add, Update, or Delete File operations.
- dryRun: Preview only (default: false).

Use this when a Codex-family model emits its native apply_patch grammar. Use edit for targeted find-and-replace edits.

patch.description: OpenAI apply_patch block from *** Begin Patch to *** End Patch

dryRun.description: Preview the patch without writing changes

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit files with find-and-replace. oldText must match exactly (whitespace, indentation, newlines).

Parameters:
- path: File path
- oldText/newText: Single edit (text to find and replacement)
- edits: Array of {oldText, newText} for multiple sequential edits (1-50)
- replaceAll: Replace all occurrences (default: false). For single edit only.
- occurrence: Which match (default: 1). For single edit only.
- dryRun: Preview only (default: false)

Use either oldText/newText OR edits array, not both.

Best practices:
- Read file first to verify exact formatting
- Include context (5-10 lines) for uniqueness
- Match indentation style (tabs vs spaces)
- Use dryRun for complex edits
- Use edits array for multiple related changes (atomic)

If "not found", read file to check actual content.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text to find and replace (must match exactly)

newText.description: New text to replace the old text with

edits.description: Multiple edits to apply sequentially (alternative to oldText/newText)

oldText.description: Exact text to find and replace

newText.description: Replacement text (omit or empty string to delete)

replaceAll.description: Replace all occurrences (useful for variable renaming). Cannot be used with occurrence or edits.

occurrence.description: Which occurrence of the text to replace (1-based). Cannot be used with replaceAll or edits.

dryRun.description: Preview the diff without writing changes

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

previewDiff.description: If true, return the diff between previous content and new content (when file exists)

backup.description: If true, writes a .bak copy alongside the file before overwriting

tools.name: notebook_edit
tools.description:
Edit Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) files at the cell level.

Parameters:
- path: Path to the notebook file
- cell_id: ID of the cell to edit (optional, use cell_index if not available)
- cell_index: 0-based index of the cell (used if cell_id not provided)
- new_source: New content for the cell
- cell_type: "code" or "markdown" (required for insert, optional for replace)
- edit_mode: "replace" (default), "insert", or "delete"

Modes:
- replace: Replace cell content (default)
- insert: Insert new cell after specified cell (or at beginning if no cell specified)
- delete: Remove the specified cell (new_source is ignored)

Use 'read' tool first to view notebook structure and get cell IDs/indices.

path.description: Path to the Jupyter notebook file (.ipynb)

cell_id.description: Cell ID to edit. For insert mode, new cell is inserted after this cell. Omit to insert at beginning.

cell_index.description: Cell index (0-based) to edit. Used if cell_id is not provided.

new_source.description: The new source content for the cell

cell_type.description: Cell type (code or markdown). Required for insert mode, defaults to current type for replace.

edit_mode.description: Edit mode: replace (default), insert (add new cell), or delete (remove cell)

tools.name: todo
tools.description:
Track tasks for coding sessions. Use for complex, multi-step work to demonstrate progress.

When to use:
- 3+ steps or non-trivial work
- User requests multiple tasks
- After receiving new instructions

When NOT to use:
- Single, straightforward tasks
- Trivial work (<3 steps)
- Conversational requests

Task states:
- pending: Not started
- in_progress: Currently working (ONE AT A TIME)
- completed: Finished

Management:
- Mark in_progress BEFORE starting work
- Mark completed IMMEDIATELY when done
- Only ONE in_progress task at a time
- Use 'updates' to modify existing tasks by id

Call this tool IN PARALLEL with other tools to save time.

content.description: Human readable description of the task

status.description: Current progress state of the task

anyOf.description: JSON stringified array of TodoWrite-style task objects

updates.description: Updates to apply to existing tasks (identified by their id)

id.description: Identifier of the task to update

notes.description: Replace notes associated with the task

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description:
Ask the user structured questions with predefined options.

Use this tool when you need to:
- Gather user preferences or requirements
- Clarify ambiguous instructions
- Get decisions on implementation choices
- Offer choices about direction to take

Parameters:
- questions: Array of 1-4 questions, each with:
  - question: The full question text
  - header: Short label (max 12 chars) like "Library", "Approach"
  - options: 2-4 choices with label and description
  - options[].preview: Optional markdown/text/diff preview for concrete artifacts
  - multiSelect: Allow multiple selections (default: false)

An "Other" option is automatically added to allow custom input.
Users can respond with option numbers, labels, or free text.
Preview HTML is not supported; use markdown, text, or diff so clients can render previews safely.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. E.g., "Which library should we use for date formatting?"

header.description: Short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). E.g., "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: Available choices (2-4 options). Each should be distinct. An 'Other' option is automatically added.

label.description: The display text for this option (1-5 words). Should clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen.

kind.description: Preview format. Raw HTML is intentionally unsupported; use markdown, text, or diff.

body.description: Preview content shown with the option. Keep it focused; large artifacts should be summarized.

multiSelect.description: Allow selecting multiple options. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.
